_comment: R1a spine roster (planning/prompts/01a-spine-roster.md). Two kinds only: schema rows (few - 00's named six plus the four safety domains) and template rows (organizational situations pointing at exactly one schema). Work types, file formats, residual homes, and groups are NOT rows (CONNECTION.md section 2 node test). The template count deliberately stops UNDER 00's roughly-200-300 target: with ten schemas, only this many situations are honest - the arithmetic and the refused holes are in ROSTER.md. parent_id is everywhere null: PR-5 leaves browse shelving to R1c. must_consider_residuals uses section-7.3's nine names, 00's spelling. Every threshold is an injected slot; this file holds no numbers.

nodes.name: Academic
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Academic fact schema: school, term, subject (D6: the stored key for 00's 'course'), instructor, work_type. Work types (syllabus, homework, lecture) are VALUES of work_type, never nodes.

nodes.name: College applications
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Applications fact schema: target_university, application_cycle, application_document_type, purpose. purpose lives ONLY here (PR-1). Role split: target_university vs school.

nodes.name: Research
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Research fact schema: project, stage, artifact_type, lab, venue. project and artifact_type are shared with the code schema (shares_field is derived from the shared canonical reference, never authored).

nodes.name: Career and recruiting
nodes.one_line_hint: PLACEHOLDER SCHEMA - a launch domain of 00, but its field rows are deferred (S3 / D1 narrowed; owed before P10). Write NO field rows. The recorded dimension recommendation - company, then role or recruiting cycle, then document type - is held as prose until the schema lands.

nodes.name: Photos and captures
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Photos fact schema: capture_year, event, location, people, camera_information, media_type. Time-first is the recommended exception for capture media. Camera EXIF is strong photo evidence; absence of EXIF is never proof of a screenshot.

nodes.name: Code projects
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Code fact schema: project, repository, programming_language, artifact_type. Repository roots and package manifests are the anchor evidence; existing project structure is preserved, not reorganized.

nodes.name: Finance
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's Finance fact schema: institution, account_type, tax_year, record_type - a SAFETY domain whose four fields extract at launch under local-only rules (PR-2). Detect and protect before any cloud or automated placement decision.

nodes.name: Identity
nodes.one_line_hint: PLACEHOLDER SAFETY SCHEMA - detects and protects identity material (passports, IDs, credentials); writes NO field rows (D1 narrowed / PR-6). Falls through to Protected Records; content never reaches a cloud prompt.

nodes.name: Medical
nodes.one_line_hint: PLACEHOLDER SAFETY SCHEMA - detects and protects medical material; writes NO field rows (D1 narrowed / PR-6). Co-activates with finance on healthcare-insurance material via also_holds_with (PR-8).

nodes.name: Legal
nodes.one_line_hint: PLACEHOLDER SAFETY SCHEMA - detects and protects legal material; writes NO field rows (D1 narrowed / PR-6). Falls through to Protected Records.

nodes.name: Coursework (taking a course)
nodes.one_line_hint: The Academic schema's default situation: files a student produces or receives by taking one course in one term. Recommended dimensions are 00's own - school, term, subject, work_type. Owns syllabus PDFs, lecture decks, and course .ics invites (calendar is file_kind_plausible only, never sufficient alone).

nodes.name: Teaching a course
nodes.one_line_hint: The instructor's side of one course: teaching materials, rosters (privacy: other people's data), gradebooks. Same schema as coursework - PR-7 forbids a second schema; the differing detection signals and dimension recommendation are what license this row.

nodes.name: K-12 schooling records
nodes.one_line_hint: Report cards, enrollment forms, school communications for primary and secondary schooling - often held by a parent about a child (subject is not the holder; privacy rules differ from coursework).

nodes.name: IEP and accommodation plans
nodes.one_line_hint: Individualized education programs and accommodation records - a coverage gap the overnight pass missed. Sensitive child records crossing education and medical; privacy rules dominate.

nodes.name: Continuing education and certification courses
nodes.one_line_hint: Professional development coursework: provider courses, CE credits, completion certificates. school holds the provider value.

nodes.name: Online course (MOOC)
nodes.one_line_hint: Platform-based self-paced study (a gap the overnight pass missed): downloaded lectures, exercises, completion certificates; often no term. school holds the platform or provider value.

nodes.name: Homeschooling
nodes.one_line_hint: Parent-run schooling (a gap the overnight pass missed): curricula, worksheets, portfolios, assessment records; the holder is teacher and administrator at once.

nodes.name: Study abroad term
nodes.one_line_hint: One term at another institution: two school values in play, travel and visa material nearby (identity neighbors), credit-transfer paperwork.

nodes.name: Standardized testing
nodes.one_line_hint: Test prep and score reports (SAT, GRE, TOEFL shapes). subject holds the test name as a value. Score reports also serve application packets - consider also_holds_with college_applications.

nodes.name: Transcripts, diplomas and credentials
nodes.one_line_hint: Official academic records: registrar language, seals, verification codes. Grades are sensitive. A transcript may belong to several application packets at once - membership is multi-valued, the fact set is one.

nodes.name: Recommendation letters written
nodes.one_line_hint: A recommender's own letter files about other people (privacy: subjects are not the holder). Received recommendations live inside application packets as application_document_type values, not here.

nodes.name: Undergraduate application (institution-first)
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's default Applications situation: target institution, then application cycle, then document type. Essays, portal records, checklists, supporting materials. A conflicting target institution is an outlier, never silently absorbed.

nodes.name: Purpose-defined application packet
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's own second branch pattern: one flat purpose-coherent packet (the Chinese University Application Materials example) - transcript, ID, personal statement, resume, certificate, abstract kept together because they were submitted together. Owns submission-archive evidence (submission.zip is 00's own example).

nodes.name: Graduate and professional school application
nodes.one_line_hint: Same field set as undergraduate, different detection: statements of purpose, CVs, writing samples, program-specific portals, funding questions.

nodes.name: K-12 and secondary school admission
nodes.one_line_hint: School admission packets held by a parent: forms, assessments, interviews. Child data - privacy rules differ from the adult default.

nodes.name: Scholarship and fellowship applications
nodes.one_line_hint: Application packets addressed to a sponsoring organization. NOTE the field tension: target_university would hold a sponsor that is not a university - recorded in ROSTER.md, do not mint a new field to fix it.

nodes.name: Research project workspace
nodes.one_line_hint: The Research schema's default situation: one project's working materials arranged project, then stage, then artifact_type (00's own recommendation).

nodes.name: Manuscript preparation and publication
nodes.one_line_hint: Drafts, submission packets, referee reports, revision letters, proofs - heavy version families, venue-scoped correspondence.

nodes.name: Conference abstracts, posters and talks
nodes.one_line_hint: Venue-scoped research outputs: abstracts, posters, slide decks, registration and travel context nearby. Owns presentation decks.

nodes.name: Lab notebooks, protocols and experiment records
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's research-and-lab-work launch face: notebooks, SOPs, instrument output, sample records. Detection differs sharply from manuscript material.

nodes.name: Datasets and analysis work
nodes.one_line_hint: Datasets, analysis code, computational notebooks, results tables. Strong also_holds candidate with the code schema (shared project and artifact_type keys). Owns research spreadsheets.

nodes.name: Grant proposals and funding
nodes.one_line_hint: Proposals, budgets (finance neighbor), sponsor correspondence, progress reports - deadline-driven packets per sponsor and project.

nodes.name: Ethics, IRB and consent materials
nodes.one_line_hint: Approvals, consent forms, participant-facing materials. Human-subjects privacy rules dominate; participant data may cross into medical safety territory.

nodes.name: Literature and reading library
nodes.one_line_hint: Papers BY OTHERS collected for reading: DOIs, no authorship link to the holder. The canonical falls-through case: with no active project association the honest home is the Reading Inbox residual.

nodes.name: Thesis or dissertation
nodes.one_line_hint: A degree-defining research project: chapters, committee feedback, defense materials, submission formalities. School context is real but the organizing facts are project ones.

nodes.name: Recruiting and job search
nodes.one_line_hint: The Career default situation (a 00 launch domain): applications to companies, offer letters, interview prep and scheduling (recruiting email is a real file kind here). Dimension recommendation held as prose until the career schema lands (PR-6): company, then role or recruiting cycle, then document type. Resume is a document/version family, never a template of its own.

nodes.name: Employment records at one employer
nodes.one_line_hint: Onboarding paperwork, contracts, performance reviews, separation records for a job held. Higher privacy than recruiting; payroll slips belong to the finance neighbor.

nodes.name: Consulting and client engagements
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's client-engagements situation: proposals, statements of work, deliverables per client. The our_firm vs client role split is the load-bearing field distinction; invoicing is the finance neighbor.

nodes.name: Portfolio and work samples
nodes.one_line_hint: Curated work samples and case studies assembled to showcase - the purpose (showing) differs from the projects the samples came from. Owns design/creative source files (PSD, AI, CAD shapes) until a creative schema exists (refused hole - see ROSTER.md).

nodes.name: Professional licenses, certifications and memberships
nodes.one_line_hint: Credential records: license certificates, renewal notices, membership confirmations. Distinct from the coursework that earned them (academic.continuing-education neighbor).

nodes.name: Hiring as the employer
nodes.one_line_hint: The other side of recruiting: requisitions, candidate packets, scorecards. Almost entirely OTHER PEOPLE'S data - privacy rules are the point of this row.

nodes.name: Camera photos by event
nodes.one_line_hint: The Photos schema's default situation and 00's own template: year, then event. Camera EXIF, GPS and capture time drive deterministic event proposals. Owns the image family including HEIC (00: HEIC support is explicit, not optional).

nodes.name: Screenshots
nodes.one_line_hint: ALIGNMENT's own second-situation example (photo-event vs screenshot-capture). A screenshot is always a screenshot OF something - OCR is how it becomes legible; absence of EXIF is never proof. Conflicting signals abstain. Falls through to Temporary Screenshots.

nodes.name: Scans and photographed documents
nodes.one_line_hint: Captures whose content is a document: photographed pages, scanner output, no-text-layer PDFs routed to OCR. Usually re-routes to another domain once OCR yields facts; media_type records the capture nature.

nodes.name: Family photo archive
nodes.one_line_hint: Inherited and re-scanned family photographs: unreliable or absent EXIF, decade-level dating, people-heavy (people stays a search field, not a folder level, pending Joseph).

nodes.name: Trip photographs
nodes.one_line_hint: Photos of one trip: event holds the trip value (Japan Trip 2025 is 00's own value example), location and capture_year reinforce. The records half of travel lives on the finance schema (travel.bookings-confirmations) - see ROSTER.md NEEDS-JOSEPH on whether travel deserves its own small schema.

nodes.name: Personal video and audio recordings
nodes.one_line_hint: Home movies, voice memos, event recordings: duration and container metadata, capture time when present. Speech-to-text only under an explicit privacy and compute policy (00). Owns the audio_video family.

nodes.name: Drone and aerial captures
nodes.one_line_hint: A coverage gap the overnight pass missed: drone stills and footage with flight-log metadata, aerial GPS tracks; media_type distinguishes them inside photo events.

nodes.name: Social platform exports
nodes.one_line_hint: Takeout-style bundles (a gap the overnight pass missed): platform export structure mixing media with JSON sidecars. Detection is the export layout itself; capture facts come from sidecar metadata, not file timestamps.

nodes.name: Messenger and chat exports
nodes.one_line_hint: iMessage/WhatsApp-shaped exports (a gap the overnight pass missed): conversation archives with embedded media. Correspondence is potentially sensitive; privacy rules dominate; contact identities stay protected.

nodes.name: Software project
nodes.one_line_hint: The Code schema's default situation and a 00 launch domain: a repository-rooted project recognized by structural markers (package manifests, repo roots). Existing project structure is preserved - dependency trees are excluded, never proposed as destinations. Owns code_structured, structural filesystem evidence, and source archives.

nodes.name: Notebooks and ML experiments
nodes.one_line_hint: Computational notebooks, experiment runs, model and dataset artifacts. The strongest also_holds candidate with research (shared project and artifact_type keys).

nodes.name: Scratch scripts and prototypes
nodes.one_line_hint: Loose code files with no repository root: one-off scripts, downloaded snippets, prototypes. The honest destination is often the Review Later residual, not an invented project.

nodes.name: Dotfiles and environment configuration
nodes.one_line_hint: Shell configs, editor settings, environment files. Configs can embed credentials - privacy rules matter more than folder shape; secrets route to identity safety handling.

nodes.name: Personal knowledge vault
nodes.one_line_hint: Obsidian/Notion-shaped markdown vaults (a gap the overnight pass missed): vault markers and wiki-links are the repo-root analogue. The product's job is to detect and PRESERVE the vault as a structural unit, never to scatter its notes.

nodes.name: Personal financial records
nodes.one_line_hint: The Finance schema's default situation: statements and account documents arranged institution, then account_type, with tax_year for year-scoped records. Safety domain: local-only extraction, protection before any cloud or placement path.

nodes.name: Tax filings by year
nodes.one_line_hint: Year-first is the honest exception for tax material: tax_year, then record_type. Jurisdiction-specific form NAMES are values (D4, R5's catalogue) - never field names, never dimensions.

nodes.name: Receipts and personal expenses
nodes.one_line_hint: Receipt-shaped records: purchase confirmations, delivery notices, e-receipts arriving by email. Isolated ones fall through to the Receipts and Confirmations residual rather than forcing an account association.

nodes.name: Investment and brokerage accounts
nodes.one_line_hint: Brokerage statements, trade confirmations, cost-basis and retirement account records - tax_year matters at filing time.

nodes.name: Loans and mortgages
nodes.one_line_hint: Loan applications, closing packets (legal neighbor), servicing statements, payoff records.

nodes.name: Personal insurance policies and claims
nodes.one_line_hint: PR-8: an individual's policies and claims over the Finance vocabulary - institution, then record_type. One of three insurance SITUATIONS on one schema, never three schema slugs.

nodes.name: Corporate insurance
nodes.one_line_hint: PR-8: a firm's coverage, certificates and claims - institution, then record_type, then tax_year.

nodes.name: Health insurance coverage and claims
nodes.one_line_hint: PR-8: cards, EOBs, claims over the Finance vocabulary. Where it touches medical material the medical safety placeholder co-activates via also_holds_with - and still writes no fields (PR-6).

nodes.name: Cryptocurrency and digital assets
nodes.one_line_hint: A coverage gap the overnight pass missed: exchange statements, wallet exports, transaction CSVs. Wallet credentials and seed phrases are identity-safety material, never filed as finance records.

nodes.name: Small-business bookkeeping
nodes.one_line_hint: Invoices issued and received, ledgers, expense reports for a person's own small operation. Owns working spreadsheets. Client identity ties to the career consulting neighbor.

nodes.name: Cap tables and equity paperwork
nodes.one_line_hint: A coverage gap the overnight pass missed: option grants, SAFEs, valuation reports, equity statements - finance vocabulary with legal neighbors and high sensitivity.

nodes.name: Student financial aid and loans
nodes.one_line_hint: Aid applications, award letters, loan servicing - finance vocabulary even though the material orbits academic life (academic and college_applications neighbors).

nodes.name: Travel bookings and confirmations
nodes.one_line_hint: Itineraries, boarding passes, reservation confirmations - transactional records with an issuing institution and a record_type. The trip itself is a P9 group or user folder for now: neither photos nor finance can express trip-then-record-type (recorded NEEDS-JOSEPH). Isolated items fall through to Receipts and Confirmations, as 00's own examples do.

nodes.name: Subscriptions, utilities and recurring bills
nodes.one_line_hint: 00's personal-administration face: utility accounts, subscription confirmations, recurring billing - institution, then record_type.

nodes.name: Vehicle ownership and service records
nodes.one_line_hint: Purchase, registration, service and insurance records for a vehicle - record_type over the finance vocabulary with legal and identity neighbors for titles.

nodes.name: Home and property records
nodes.one_line_hint: Purchase or sale packets, tenancy, improvement receipts, warranties - household administration over the finance vocabulary; leases are the legal neighbor's material.

nodes.name: HOA and residents' association records
nodes.one_line_hint: A coverage gap the overnight pass missed: dues, notices, covenants, meeting minutes from a homeowners' or residents' association - institution holds the association value.

nodes.name: Payroll and income records received
nodes.one_line_hint: Pay stubs, income statements, employer year-end forms (form NAMES are jurisdiction values, D4). Sits between employment (career neighbor) and tax filings.

nodes.name: Core identity documents
nodes.one_line_hint: Passports, national IDs, birth and citizenship certificates - 00's protected-state material: enter protection immediately, never a cloud prompt, fall through to Protected Records when no deeper accepted group exists. Owns contact-file evidence (.vcf): privacy-protected, never a folder proposal.

nodes.name: Immigration and visa paperwork
nodes.one_line_hint: Visa applications, permits, entry records - purpose-coherent packets outside admissions (PR-1: no purpose clone; the packet activates on its own evidence or falls through). Crosses identity and legal safety domains.

nodes.name: Credentials and password-manager exports
nodes.one_line_hint: A coverage gap the overnight pass missed: password-manager exports, recovery codes, keys, encrypted containers. Maximum sensitivity; owns the opaque_binary family (encrypted or unreadable material is represented, not forced open).

nodes.name: Personal health records
nodes.one_line_hint: Portal exports, lab results, prescriptions, visit summaries - 00's protected-state material. The medical schema writes no fields (PR-6); this row's research is detection and protection, not extraction.

nodes.name: A dependant's health records
nodes.one_line_hint: Health records held FOR another person (child or dependant adult): the holder-vs-subject role distinction is the point; consent and privacy rules differ from one's own records.

nodes.name: Wearable and health-app exports
nodes.one_line_hint: Health-app export bundles (a gap the overnight pass missed): structured XML/JSON archives of vitals and activity. Bulk-sensitive even when each datum looks trivial.

nodes.name: Personal legal matters
nodes.one_line_hint: Disputes, court correspondence, notarized documents held by an individual - 00's protected-state material; the legal schema writes no fields (PR-6).

nodes.name: Wills, estate and end-of-life documents
nodes.one_line_hint: Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, advance directives (medical neighbor). Among the most sensitive material a corpus holds.

nodes.name: Leases and signed agreements
nodes.one_line_hint: Signed contracts an individual is party to: leases, service agreements, employment contracts (career neighbor). Isolated signed PDFs otherwise land in Independent Records.

nodes.name: Law-practice matter file
nodes.one_line_hint: A practitioner's matter/case files - the professional situation the overnight pass expanded into dozens of sibling schemas. One placeholder row: research detection and privacy; field rows stay unwritten (PR-6). Client-confidential by default.
